en: Oṃ, salutations to Śiva. Oṃ, salutations to Sarasvatī. Oṃ, salutations to the Guru. Oṃ, may there be prosperity.

Oṃ, on the beautiful peak of Kailāsa, adorned with various jewels, Caṇḍikā questioned Bhairava with supreme devotion. Oṃ, the illustrious Caṇḍikā. Oṃ, [to] Tripurā... (Note: The provided text fragment ends abruptly; the translation reflects the portion available.)
[The people] especially [desire] the Lord of Men’s gold and jewels. In the Kali age, gold and jewels become as precious as gold; by what means, O Goddess, can one obtain gold, jewels, and the like?
This has been declared in all the scriptures—tell me that, O Treasure of Compassion. Śrī Śaṅkara said:

Oṃ. Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain how one may obtain jewels and other such things. By my splendor, what cannot be obtained? Even a Kiṃnara can be won over. Listen, O Priyaṃvadā, to the method for purifying the substance of the *śaṃbala* by means of the *vallaka* in a secret manner. Vī...

One should worship Siddhakālikā according to the Ratnatantra; or else, one should worship the supreme goddess Dakṣiṇakālikā according to the procedure taught in the Kālītantra through recitation and worship for seven days. In the Satya age, [the result is] onefold, but in the Tretā age, it is twofold.
In the Dvāpara age, three [units]; one should know it thus for all [ages], and in the Kali age, one should worship with fourfold [the amount].
Having brought with great effort two *tolakas* of *śambala*, [one should worship] the seed-syllable (*bīja*) consisting of *vasu*, *āyus*, and *śiva*, adorned with *māyā* and the *bindu*.
One should recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times over the provisions; having carefully brought the milk produced from a black cow, measuring eighty tolas,
one should recite it one hundred and eight times.

Oṃ Śrīḥ Maḥ! One should place [the substance] within milk using a thread of red cloth. O wise one, having raised it, one should cook it very slowly with fire. When the liquid has been reduced by half, reaching the point where the Bindu deity and Agni remain, then one should place the substance to be weighed into the midst of the milk.
Having offered [the oblation], an examination must then be performed; one should place it upon the fire.

When the substance is seen in the smokeless fire, one should then cause it to rise. There, one should recite the mantra which possesses all auspicious characteristics, together with the copper and the fire.
One should cast it into the fire; just as with fire, so too with copper—the observer shall then cause it to rise. One should add that substance, equal in measure to a *guñjā* seed, to the powder.
Truly, truly, O Girijā, it certainly becomes silver. Oṃ Śrī.
Caṇḍikā: Oṃ! By what means did Śaṅkara milk the form of the syllable Om?
O Mahādeva, O Śaṃkara, please tell me that method out of compassion. Oṃ Śrī Śaṃkara said:
Oṃ, the wise one should bring the engraving tool and four *tolakas* of weight.
O Girijā, one should cause silver to be fashioned with parched grain (lāja) through the application of fire;
having ground it together with double the amount of mango blossom, one should perform the process of blending.
Over that, one should always recite the mantra consisting of Lakṣmaṇa, [known as] Mahāmā...
One should recite this one thousand and eight times; then, having made it into a pill,
if one causes it to be mixed [with milk], it will indeed take the form of milk— this is the truth, the absolute truth,
O Daughter of the Mountain!
She who destroys Yama, Madhu, and Kaiṭabha; she who uproots the buffalo-demon Mahiṣa;

she who crushes the fierce Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa with her fiery glances; she who devours the blood of Raktavīja; she who shatters the Daityas Sumbha and Niśumbha; she who is the Śakti; she who is Siddhalakṣmī; she who resides in the supreme abode (Parāsāda).
May the Sovereign of the Universe, accompanied by the form of the tip of a lute-string, protect me.
O fair-faced one, listen to the *oṃ* mantra, which is difficult to find even in the three worlds:

*oṃ eṃ hlīṃ klīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ namaḥ*. Following that, [there are] the source of speech (*vāgbhava*), the *māyā*, the seed-syllable of desire (*kāmabīja*), then the stable *māyā*, the great *māyā*, and *kā*.
Then, preceded by the seed-syllable *ma* and followed by *namaḥ*, one should first recite the nine-syllabled great mantra (*mahāmantra*) one hundred times.

If they recite the great mantra in reverse, one should likewise recite it one hundred times. Listen, O Goddess, I shall explain the seer (*ṛṣi*), the meter (*chandas*), and the auspicious characteristics.
Oṃ. For this great hymn of seven hundred verses (*Saptaśatī-mahāstotra*), Medhātithi is the seer (*ṛṣi*);
the Gāyatrī, Anuṣṭubh, Bṛhatī, Paṅkti, Triṣṭubh, and Jagatī are the meters (*chandas*); [and] Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī, and Mahāsarasvatī are the deities.

The seed-syllable is *eṃ hrīṃ klīṃ*, the power (*śakti*) is *kṣauṃ*, and the application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of accomplishing my [name] desire during the recitation of this hymn of praise to the deities of the *rasvatīs*.
O Great Goddess, one should perform the meditation on the six limbs with the *praṇava* (Om).
Thus, O beloved, the characteristics of the recitation of Caṇḍī have been told to you; [beginning with] "Sāvarṇi, the Sun," this is the mantra of Sāvarṇi. This is that mantra.
O Goddess, having established [the deity], one should recite it for three days or three nights; O Goddess,

there is not even a blade of grass that can harm him, whether he is afflicted by a great disease, great suffering, the terrible oppression of a king, or even when his life-force is seized by various maladies.

O Goddess of the Gods, by reciting [this] in this manner during times of fear, in the multitude of afflictions caused by planets, or even in the case of sins such as the killing of a Brahmin, one is liberated; there is no doubt in this matter. O Goddess, what more need be said? A person shall obtain all peace.
One becomes free from all fear and equal to Madana himself; O Maheśānī, even when this is performed, if peace does not arise, [then it is known].
It must be performed again by that very same person; then success will certainly be attained.
Thus ends the sixth chapter in its entirety in the Śrī Mātṛkābheda Tantra. 6.
Oṃ Śrīḥ!
Oṃ Śrī Caṇḍikā! Oṃ, by what means, O Śaṅkara, can a substance become devoid of fragrance?
"I wish to hear all of that, if you have affection for me. Śrī Śaṅkara said:

One should take the scent and recite: *Oṃ śivaṃ vahnisamārūḍhaṃ vāmanetravibhūṣitaṃ bindunādasamāyuktam*. Having rolled [the mantra] over the word and uttered it one hundred and eight times, there truly arises at that very moment the destruction of foul odors and the like.
[Thus ends the first chapter of the Śrīmātṛkātantra-bheda]. 1. Oṃ, the illustrious Goddess.

Oṃ! Speak, O Lord, Omniscient One, supreme among those who know all principles! O Protector, regarding that which was spoken by You concerning the play of equal emanation: how is a son born, and where does the seed reside?
How does the ever-increasing *liṅga* come to be, or how does its entry occur?
"O Lord, I am indeed bound; protect me from this peril of suffering! Om Śaṅkara! Om!
In the city of Maṇipūra, situated in the center of the great lotus within the Suṣumṇā, is that illuminating deity.
There is a captivating navel-cavity, endowed with eight petals and eternally adorned by the Liberated Ones."

As his pair of testicles grew day by day in this manner, a beautiful stalk (nāla) emerged from the middle, circular in shape and very cooling (another reading is *suśītala*). Its tip was not bent, and its middle was always filled with bliss, O Śivā.
Listen, O beautiful and auspicious one of lovely limbs; within that, behold the Liṅga.
That form which is supreme bliss exists there in the three worlds. Listen with a concentrated mind to the nature of the navel-lotus:
it is the station of the Bindu in the central region, eternally adorned with lotuses, located in the outer...

Outside of that, there is an eight-petaled lotus and a square; it is provided with four gates, radiant like gold, and circular. Upon its petals should be flowers joined with a dot (bindu), five on each petal.
(Variegated:

On the outer petals of the fully blossomed lotus, there is an even greater vision; O Great Lord, if within that [lotus] there were the state of being a *liṅga*, then the thread situated in the middle of the lotus would be the continuity (*santati*).
From that it arises; for the sake of the person’s non-distinct object, the power [of speech] becomes superior through speech.

Then the goddess becomes a maiden, and in the opposite case, she becomes a man. When there is an equal union of both, it certainly results in a Kṛṣṇa. Listen, O beautiful-limbed and fortunate one, to the supreme majesty of the flower; when joined in this union, it increases day by day.

When two months have passed, that [seed] becomes joined with its flower; then, from the Supreme Lord, the continuity [of the lineage] becomes manifest. When some disease or the like arises, or when [insects such as] moths and the like occur, the life-force (jīva) is destroyed; so too is the life-force of the woman.

Thus it is said: Oṃ Śrī Śaṅkara! Oṃ! How can I describe the greatness of that flower? It is not even a thousandth part of it, O beloved, within the midst of that flower. Where bubbles abide, there indeed shall be progeny; in this great, expanding flower.
Not even the slightest pain shall arise. O Mistress of the Gods, in this manner, a lineage of a thousand shall come into being. O Great Goddess, strive diligently to sport with me;
from such sporting, a son shall be born, who is celebrated as Gaṇeśa. Furthermore, O Supreme Goddess, he shall be your son.
Through your grace, creation shall arise upon the earth as is fitting, free from all obstacles.

Having heard this, O Great Goddess, the Goddess, overwhelmed by the fire of passion, embraced Śiva; and Śiva also became equanimous. [Thus ends the second chapter in the glorious Mātṛkā-tantra. 2. Om, salutations to Mātṛkā.

Oṃ Oṃ Śrī Devī: "Oṃ, it has been heard everywhere that enjoyment (*bhoga*) is the giver of happiness even to the Moon, the Lord; yet one attains liberation through enjoyment. How is this so? Tell me, O Knower of Yoga. Oṃ Śaṅkara:

Through enjoyment one attains yoga; through enjoyment, the practice of the Kula; through enjoyment one obtains siddhi, and through enjoyment one may attain liberation. Therefore, O beloved, having performed the external worship according to the ritual, listen to the rule for eating, which is the station of yoga.

From the *mūlādhāra*, the *kuṇḍalinī*— whose form is like a coiled serpent (*bhujaṅga*), endowed with qualities, and consisting of the forms of the moon, sun, and fire— is the individual soul (*jīvātman*) that always resides within the Supreme Lord. One should contemplate this goddess as she descends from the *mūlādhāra* and reaches the tip of the tongue.
The wise practitioner should place purified fish, meat, and other offerings before her mouth;
having uttered the root mantra, he should offer them into the mouth of Kuṇḍalinī. By this rite, the Goddess shall gather all speech, and Kuṇḍalī shall consume it.

For one who meditates on the Goddess Nīdevī with unwavering thought, there shall be accomplishment in mantra, and likewise accomplishment in gnosis (jñāna); otherwise it is not so. When this is done, he becomes Śiva in the form of Brahmā and Hari himself in the form of Viṣṇu; for him there shall be accomplishment in yoga and the eight supernatural powers (aṣṭasiddhi) will come to pass.

Even if enemies were to give one dreadful, artificial poison to be consumed, by which the Goddess [bestows] immortality without a doubt, one should purify that substance with the mantra; it will become nectar in that very instant. At that same time, the Kālakūṭa arose from the churning of the ocean.
"O beloved, by churning through that practice, that poison has been consumed by me;

for the goddess Kāṇḍalinī, who is the supreme power (Kalā), is enjoyed. Even poison becomes nectar in the form of the Sun—this, O Goddess, is what I have told you regarding the nature of the ritual of eating."
"O Maheśāna, by whom must all this be protected when one is beset by the danger of the bound souls (paśu)? Śrī Devī asked.

"Oṃ! Listen, O Lord, whose nature is the Supreme Bliss and the essence of both the Transcendent and the Immanent (Parāpara-kula)! Speak, O Wise One, what is the form of the *homakanda* of Īśāna? Oṃ! Śrī Śaṅkara replied: "Oṃ!
Outside of Maṇipūra, there is the beautiful navel-lotus, which likewise possesses eight petals."
(Variegated):

O Lord of Gods, that which is difficult to obtain among the circular, square, and other types of sacrificial pits (*kuṇḍa*) is the *kāmarūpaka* pit; O Lord of Gods, it is the creator of all sacrificial pits for the Brahmins.
A circular pit is prescribed for the Vaiśya of many castes, while a semi-circular pit adorned with a triangle is proclaimed for Śūdras. Thus,
O Great Goddess, the pit is adorned with these three [shapes] and possesses an upward-pointing neck.
O Śivā, the central stalk of the navel region is adorned with the supreme nectar in the thousand-petaled lotus;
the beautiful Mūlādhārī embraces that central stalk, which consists of perpetual bliss. O Goddess, this is the sacrificial pit (*homakuṇḍa*) according to all tantras.

It is traditionally taught that by the grace of this oblation (*homa*), one becomes directly composed of Brahman. Furthermore, regarding the oblation in the *homa*, it should be understood that there are four [oblations] for a Brāhmaṇa,
three for a Kṣatriya, two for a Vaiśya, and one divine oblation for a Śūdra.

Liberation is also fourfold: for a Brāhmaṇa it is Mahāmokṣa; for a Kṣatriya, Sāyujya; for a Vaiśya, Sārūpya; and for those born of the Śūdra caste, Sālokya. For those outside [the fold], there is the external *kuṇḍa* and the external *homa*; indeed, they are not gods.

The best of practitioners should not cause a breach of the lineage or a breach of the sacrificial pit; through external homa, the accomplishment of one's desires will surely come to pass—of this there is no doubt. Thus have I told you, O beloved.
"The supreme essence of the mantras must not be spoken before one who is ignorant; for that reason, O beloved, it has been kept secret from you.

The Śrī Devī said: "The drinking of wine is of great merit, as I have heard in all the Tantras; it has been described according to the distinctions of the *jāti* [caste/classes]. I shall now reveal it. The Śrī Śaṅkara said:
O Pārvatī, there is no doubt among the Brahmins that he is the lord of all sacrifices.

In the great Sautrāmaṇī sacrifice, the four castes beginning with the Brāhmaṇas [participate]. O Supreme Goddess, if a Brāhmaṇa speaks favorably of the drinking of wine and so forth, it constitutes a great yoga for him.
At that moment, O Daughter of the Mountain, he truly, truly becomes the very form of Śiva;
for just as water dissolves into water, as fire into fire, as the ether into the ether,
or as the beloved wind into wind— so too, O Beloved, does he merge into the Supreme Brahman.
It dissolves there; of this there is no doubt. This is the truth, the absolute truth, O Daughter of the Mountain!
Even *sāyujya* liberation is likewise ordained for Kṣatriyas and others. That woman who [attains this] through drinking in the midst [of the assembly] is indeed the Goddess herself;
of this there is no doubt. Just as fire exists within a fine thread, so does she exist within the body.

O Goddess, when the *tapas* (ascetic practice) is the object of meditation, the *bṛhatsūtra* (great thread) takes the form of worship, just as the oblation (*havis*) is offered; the wise know this as the "increasing" (*vardhamāna*). Without the middle state (*madhyamā*), the knowledge of reality (*tattvajñāna*) is not attained; therefore, the Brahmin indeed [practices] the *madhyamā*.
O Daughter of the Mountain, a Brahmin should never practice the Mother of the Vedas with effort;
for when one possesses the knowledge of Brahman, O Goddess, then he is called a Brahmin.
O Sovereign of the Kaulikas, that which is remembered in the Vedic tradition as Brahman belongs to him, [offering] oblations...

Just as fire produces a burn by its mere presence, so too, O Goddess of gods, she who bestows the knowledge of one's own kingdom through the mere release from a curse is indeed a fire. One should pay homage to such a Brāhmaṇa; he is to be known as a true Brāhmaṇa, he is an Agnihotrī.
O Goddess, he who has been initiated and serves the one composed of the three qualities (*triguṇātmaka*) is worthy of much praise;
O Goddess, he should recite for liberation and must be protected in the midst of the *paśu*s.
Through disclosure, there would be a loss of accomplishment (*siddhi*); otherwise, he is not to be censured. [Thus ends the venerable...]
[The Third Chapter in the Division of the Tṛkā Tantra] Oṃ Śrī Devī said: Oṃ!
I have heard from your mouth, O Lord of Asuras, that great liberation and the state of Nirvikalpa-Śiva are attained through the syllable Oṃ; yet, [I have heard] that Śiva is ungraspable. 3.
"O Lord, the body is ungraspable and without cause; O Mahādeva, how does the knower of Yoga speak falsely?
(Thus asked by Ghr̥tācī). Oṃ. Śrī Śiva said: "Oṃ, listen, O Goddess; I shall explain it to you. Attend with full attention and comprehend it all."

O Hero, you ask me this: "Does the individual soul (jīva) wander through eighty-four hundred thousand [births], and only then become a partaker of liberation? If there were such great knowledge within this [teaching], O Vīra...
They attain liberation at that time; for whom, then, could there be wandering?

Therefore, O Great Goddess, the Self itself is the secret light. O Supreme Lord, that speech [of Yours] is not false in its various manifestations. O Goddess, Nirvāṇa is attained through separation [from worldly bonds], and wine is the supreme cause.
O Great Goddess Caṇḍikā, without the drinking of wine, great liberation is not attained.

"Oṃ! If one dies at the Gaṅgā through ignorance [of its true nature], that very moment is liberation; for there is no cause superior to the Gaṅgā, which is difficult for others to attain. Oṃ! Śrī Śiva said:

The Goddess who consists of the fullness of Brahman is indeed Surādevī and not otherwise; therefore, she is the sixteen-fold sacrifice, Gaṅgā, and worshipped by the gods. Likewise is the Goddess Tulasī, the virtuous Satī, and the sovereign of the Asuras. And he who desires liberation should go to Mṛtyu-tīrtha.

One should perform [the ritual] with you in that same manner; likewise, in the center of the rosary, there is the great conch (*mahāśaṅkha*), which grants liberation and is the cause, O Goddess, always bestowing liberation.
Without the cause, O Goddess, there is no liberation, knowledge, and so forth. Great!
Without a conch shell and even without mantras, it bestows the perfection of mantra;
how much more so when one possesses a rosary composed of actual Brahma-grass (kuśa), which is like a great friend!
Furthermore, [this is especially true] at Śālagrāma, in Vṛndāvana, and at the Gaṅgā, which is worshipped by the gods.
Touching this great conch, it becomes the wood of touch. Oṃ Caṇḍikā. Oṃ Gaṅgā, whose water is the primal cause and the supreme cause;
if satisfaction arises from the mere touch of the cause, then [it is] Gaṅgā-spa...
"O Supreme Goddess, tell me: by mere sight [of you], one becomes like a flower made of wood;
such is the doubt in my heart. Om Śrī Śaṅkara said:
"Om, O Goddess, Mahākālī, the supreme power (parākalā), dwells in the cause; O Goddess, let the Great Knowledge (mahāvidyā) dwell [there]."

Worshipped by the gods, she is like a great conch; she who eternally possesses the form of fifty syllables is like a great conch, and this Great Vidyā is always present. Just as the touch of fire is remembered [to burn] by the mere touch of wood, so too is the touch of the Gaṅgā.
O beloved, at that very moment, Goddess Gaṅgā dissolves into the Great Conch like wood;
of this there is no doubt. Likewise, upon a stone slab, a Tulasī leaf, or other such objects, the practitioner who recites [the mantra] by the command of the Great Conch [attains the same].
Śambhu, the imperishable, dwells within the heart of that one who possesses the eight supernatural powers (*aṣṭasiddhi*);
for him, what need is there for a station on the Gaṅgā, since the Gaṅgā resides upon his crest?
Vārāṇasī is his great horse, and Haridvāra and Prayāga are his [other steeds].

Gaṇḍakī, Badarīdevī, and the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean—by the mere sight of his great conch of devotion, one obtains the fruit of all sacred pilgrimage sites; of this there is no doubt. Thus have I told you.

O Supreme Goddess, that essence of beauty, most difficult to attain, which is not to be spoken of to a beast or a blind man—this is your life-force. [Om. Thus ends the fourth chapter in the venerable Mātṛkā-tantra.
4. Om.
Śrī Oṃ Śrī Caṇḍikā! Oṃ! By what means did Śaṅkara prepare the mercury-ash? I desire to hear that, if you have any compassion for me. Oṃ.

Śrī Śaṅkara said: Oṃ! The preparation of mercury and ash, which holds various sciences and so forth, should first bring about peace according to the tantras; one should increase the merit of the performer of the rite, the best of the twice-born, by means of the procedure to be described hereafter, bestowing enjoyment and that which is to be enjoyed.
O Goddess of the gods, the Lord of the Asuras, one should offer the *madhuparka*; O Queen of the gods, one should bathe [the deity] with the five nectars (*pañcāmṛta*) and pure water.
One should present a pair of articles appropriate for the person;
having adorned a silver or copper pedestal four finger-breadths in width, [one should proceed].

One should offer what is appropriate for the person; or one should give water along with flowers dyed with lac to Śivā. O Goddess of the Gods, one should repeatedly perform the six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga) with the sacrificial ladle (sruva), and likewise offer a lamp filled with ghee, O source of auspiciousness.

Having prepared various delightful food offerings (naivedya) accompanied by diverse fruits, one should present milk-pudding (pāyasa) mixed with sugar. O beloved Maheshani, one should offer water combined with Vijaya; [reciting] the great six-syllabled mantra ending in "Gaja" (Hara).

The excellent practitioner should recite [the mantra] one thousand times; its accomplishment will certainly come to pass. Alternatively, O Supreme Lord, one should worship the goddess who bestows wealth with great effort using the sixteen types of offerings, and the wise one should recite it for twelve days.

Then one should recite the mantra a thousand times; O Maheśānī, the wise practitioner should perform a fire sacrifice (*homa*) consisting of a tenth part of that. If one is unable to perform the rite of *homa*, one should perform double the recitation.
If she is thus pleased, what indeed cannot be obtained? O Vatsā! (Note: *Vatsā* is a term of endearment used by a teacher for a disciple.)
O Goddess, having contemplated that [sacred site] which is the source of wealth for Kubera and other lords of the supreme Ishana,
and having given a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) to the Guru according to the extent of one's means, the practitioner of mantra will then become a Siddha; there is no doubt in this matter.

[The inquiry regarding the investigation of conduct. Caṇḍikā said: "O God of gods, what is the procedure for the rite of preparing sacred ash (bhasman), by which means that ash, when honored, becomes manifest in its true form? Oṃ. Śrī Śaṅkara said: "Oṃ. Having brought [the materials]..."

One should place mercury upon it and gaze at it; then, O Goddess of the Gods, one should recite the mantra consisting of the characteristics of Śarva six thousand times over it with the qualities of a practitioner. One should recite it while [the mercury] is contained in a beautiful vessel joined with *svayambhū* flowers.
Having placed the Goddess in two clay vessels resembling [the moon],
one should tie them with a thread adorned with flowers; then,
O Supreme Goddess, one should apply an ointment of five types of earth and grain.

With great effort, one should cause it to become fierce and dry; then the wise one should heat it again and cast it into the fire. On the eighth or ninth lunar day, at night, one should never cast [it] at any time. Oṃ Śrīśaṃjñikā.
Oṃ! O Lord, what is the self-arisen (*svayambhū*) like? And what is the *kuṇḍagolaka* like? O Lord, what is the "own-flower" (*svapuṣpa*) like?
And what is the "vajra-flower" (*vajrapuṣpa*) like? O Śaṅkara, tell me, O Lord, what is that which arises at all times like?
Oṃ! The illustrious Śaṅkara replied: It is devoid of marriage.
O Maheśānī, that blood of hers, when united with the first meaning of the *tāka* [mantra],
is undoubtedly self-arisen (*svayambhū*) in this place. O Śivā, if there is a maiden who has not yet had intercourse with another man, the *kuṇḍapuṣpa* arising from her is effective for all purposes.

O Goddess of the gods, the Golapuṣpa flower produced from the corpse of a man who has died while embracing another woman is supremely effective for subjugating deities. O Maheśānī, the blood of a maiden who has not yet married, collected during her first menstrual period along with her own menstrual flow, [is likewise powerful].
That which arises from the striking of a married maiden by a man is proclaimed as *mohana-vajra*. Whatever [menstrual blood] occurs every month for a married maiden, that which arises at all times—
O Goddess worshipped by heroes, the *vaṃpuṣpa* has been described; for seven nights, one should place it with great effort in the midst of fire.
Having lifted it up and placed that substance in a golden vessel, O Supreme Goddess, one should then recite the great mantra called *prasāda*. Thereafter—

The practitioner of mantra shall become accomplished; otherwise, it is not as I have spoken. O Maheśāni, having recited this mantra one thousand times, one should thereafter worship an earthen Śiva-liṅga. Then the test must be performed; listen, O Prāṇa!
O Beloved, if one places two *tolakas* of pure copper in the midst of fire and, while it is still hot,
drops into that copper a substance weighing one *guñjā*, O Supreme Goddess, it will certainly become gold at that very moment; indeed, that substance [weighing] one *guñjā* is like a lotus.

If he performs it, he becomes free from all diseases and becomes like Madana (the god of love). For him who lives long, there shall be the accomplishment of mantras. O Supreme Goddess, if he penetrates a hundred women every day, his virility and so forth remain unimpaired, and his vital energy remains undiminished.
I do not see anything else that brings about supreme growth after death as much as being endowed with meditation;

even Kubera is surpassed by his wealth when he gazes upon him. I know him to be the four-faced Brahmā in person, and like Indra in bestowing gifts, he is like Maheśvara among yogis when he has passed away.
He is exceedingly difficult to restrain, possessing a great mouth, great heroism, and a great splendor that shines brilliantly;
he has a vast chest and is devoted to the welfare of all living beings.
O Goddess, what more need be said? He is the perfect leader of those who drink [the nectar]. Thus [ends] the Śrīmātṛ...
In the Kābheda Tantra, the fifth chapter [ends]. 5. Oṃ, the Goddess said:
Oṃ! I speak, O Īśāna, omniscient one, best among those who know all tantras:

in the face of great disease, great suffering, and the peril of great poverty; for one afflicted by various torments, in the midst of various afflictions and perils, and in the destruction of kings, the fear of kings, and imprisonment.
Furthermore, O Lord of Gods, tell me, O Master, by what means can one who is afflicted by the king's punishment or likewise by the torment of malevolent planets be quickly liberated? Speak, O Lord!
Oṃ Śiva said: Oṃ Listen, O beautiful-limbed and auspicious one, to that which you ask me; I shall explain it all to you—listen with focused attention.
That which is the supreme primordial knowledge (vidyā), the other Cāmuṇḍā, Kālikā, her [application]...
"What is accomplished on the surface of the earth by merely going [there]? The Śrī Devī said: "Oṃ!
O Supreme Lord, he is everywhere proclaimed as a Caṇḍāla. O God, how is that a meritorious time when the sun has passed over it, and likewise, O Protector, when the moon [has done so]?"
Tell me this without doubt in your heart; afterwards, O Parānanda, reveal it elsewhere.

Om. Śrī Śiva said: Om. Listen, O beautiful-limbed one, O auspicious lady; [I shall speak of] the most excellent among the planets, O Goddess—the threefold nature of the planets, beginning with the Moon and the Sun.
The power (Śakti) is of the nature of fire; fire resides in the forehead and the eyes in every way.

Likewise, the Moon resides in the left eye, and when she is satisfied, she stands in the right. When the Lord Sambhunātha is made the crest-jewel [of the head], at that very moment, O Goddess, he is joined with Śakti and [the eclipse] is grasped.

O Parameśvarī, when one kisses the left eye of the Dāśī, what is the grasping of the syllable *ca*? When one kisses the forehead, there is the grasping of the fire (*agni*). O Sureśvarī, Śiva impregnates the fire;
therefore, time is the union of Śiva and Śakti.

O Śivā, one should not deliberate upon the nature of the zodiac signs and so forth as being composed of Brahman; O Maheśānī, the calculation of the zodiac signs and other such matters is merely the beautiful tradition of the Yavanas.
O Parameśvarī, the conjunction of lunar mansions, asterisms, and yogas—O Supreme Goddess—is to be understood in that very same way.

One should perform the counting of breaths without expectation; the union of Śiva and Śakti is the entire world consisting of Brahman. O Supreme Goddess, there is no need for the recitation of months, fortnights, or lunar days; by mere sight, that which is unaccomplished shall certainly become accomplished.

O Goddess worshipped by heroes, that which is to be known as the supreme *akālī* at that time—whatever karma is performed therein, one obtains its fruit within. O Sovereign of the Gods, this must not be spoken in the presence of an initiate (*paśu*), for even if your life-breath departs; with effort, the practitioner (*sādhaka*) understands this reality (*tattva*) through Brahmā. It is well-guarded.
O Pārvatī, [it arises] effortlessly, as if from its own source. The Illustrious Goddess said:
"O Supreme Lord, what is the great mantra of Cāmuṇḍā like, or what is her mode of worship? Tell me that, O Treasure of Compassion. Oṃ Śrī Śiva said:

Listen, O beautiful one with lovely limbs, to the supreme mantra of Cāmuṇḍā, by the mere knowledge of which there is no further rebirth. O Goddess, [the mantra consists of] the pair of Kālī-bījas, followed by the Kūrma-bīja; this is the supreme three-syllabled Vidyā.

One should worship the goddess Dmācāmuṇḍākālikā with one's own mind through the sixteen pure offerings. O fair-faced one, at the conclusion of the worship, one should recite the mantra three thousand times. Furthermore, O Goddess, one should worship at night according to the five principles (pañcatattva) for the sake of accomplishment.
Who, endowed with the power of the Kula, should recite the mantra thus at night? One should indeed provide a very spacious seat suitable for the construction of the yantra;
and one should offer appropriate enjoyments and the madhuparka as prescribed for the Śakti.

O Supreme Goddess, because of this, one should likewise offer a bed for her sake as a cause of all auspiciousness; furthermore, the Goddess should be adorned with ornaments and stationed here and there,
accompanied by various delightful offerings consisting of diverse substances.
During this watch, one should offer milk-rice with sugar and worship with supreme devotion; thereafter,
the offering of the bali-oblation follows.

O Supreme Goddess, one should offer a bali offering every day, both at the beginning and at the end; when this is done, great accomplishment is attained—of this there is no doubt. One who seeks wealth obtains wealth, one who seeks a son becomes possessed of a son, and in dispute one obtains victory, being triumphant even at the royal court.

Having become victorious everywhere, he shall obtain his desired sons through the Goddess; by worshipping her, he is liberated from diseases of terrible form. He shall attain the perfection of sugarcane and all perfections—this is not otherwise. Even one who has entered a prison is liberated by her.
O Supreme Goddess, this practice, which is the very essence and extremely difficult to obtain,
has been revealed by me with great affection for you, O Mistress of the Gods. Or else, O Supreme Goddess, O Sovereign of the Gods, one should recite the *Caṇḍī* and worship the goddess Caṇḍikā.

O Goddess of the Suras, one should certainly worship the supreme Caṇḍikā with the five principles (pañcatattva) accompanied by fragrant flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, and food offerings; O Supreme Goddess, she is to be propitiated with the first substance and the like through devotion, having brought together the five principles.
Then, having performed the libation (tarpaṇa) with the *dhāya* mantra, one should pour [the water] into the *argha* vessel.
Having sprinkled [the seat] with the *argha* water, one should worship the *pīṭha-saṃvarta*.
Then, having uttered the *praṇava*, the *māyā-bīja* follows after that; [then] *prabhāmā*...

One should worship Yamā, Japā, Sūkṣmā, Viśuddhā, Ānandā, Suprabhā, Vijayā, and Sarvasiddhidā; likewise, one should recite the mantras of Śaṃṣaṇī, Ṛddhi, Padmanī, Ṛddhi, and Brahmādikā, having worshipped them with the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga).

O Maheśānī, the best of practitioners should worship the retinue, and likewise worship Indra and the others, as well as the vajra and the rest; he should worship them beginning with the *praṇava* (oṃ) and ending with *namaḥ*. Then again, O Goddess, [he should worship] Maheśānī.
One should worship with the five principles (*pañcatattva*); then, having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), one should perform the rites beginning with the *kāraṇa*.
Having drunk [the offering] oneself for that Goddess, one should recite the *Caṇḍī-sureśvarī*.
In the *Mahātmya* along with its limbs (*sāṅga*), one should cause it to fall [upon the ground], and then again restore the vital breath (*prāṇa*). Then...
One should worship the stupa according to the sequence of the celestial palaces (vimāna) and partake of the drink;
at the conclusion, one should recite the root mantra one hundred times in reverse order. If a fortunate man should obtain the yoga of devotion, then moment by moment he [attains] the seed-syllables.

O Maheśānī, having performed it thus, all accomplishments (sarvasiddhi) remain in one's hand; if one were to recite this *pāṭha*, how could I possibly describe the majesty of that recitation? O Deveśī, what need is there to mention the result of reciting it even once, let alone for the sake of attaining Brahman alone?

O Supreme Goddess, one certainly attains peace everywhere; if peace were not obtained, then my word would be false. One should first perform the worship with the sixteen types of offerings (ṣoḍaśopacāra), and secondly, one should worship with the five principles (pañcatattva).

O beloved of the Lord of Devas, the fruit that a man obtains by reciting the *Sahasrāmnāya* a thousand times is not equaled by even a sixteenth part of the fruit obtained by a single recitation of this [text]. I shall now describe its meditation (*dhyāna*), so that a person may recite it while meditating accordingly. Oṃ.

May Kha protect my mouth; may Hrīṃ protect my tongue; may the seed-syllable Śrī protect the joints; may Se protect my strength; may Sa-khphreṃ protect my two arms; may the letter Ha protect the region of my throat; may the letter Śa protect my sixteen-petaled lotus; may the letter Kṣa protect what is below that; may the letter Ma protect my heart; and may the letter La protect the region of my back.
The syllable *puṃ* is on the right side of my chest, while *śa* and *ka* are on the left side. *Tu* and *ro* are on the upper part, and *heṃ* is on the right arm;
*kṣa* is on the left hand, *ma* is on my fingers, *tū* is on my palms, and *la* is on my arms and face. *Va* is on my hair, and *ra* is on...
May *rojaṭharam* protect my belly, *oṃkāra* my pair of feet, and *klīṃ* my entire body.
May *hauṃ hauṃ* protect my genitals and all my hair; may the seed-syllable *eṃ* protect me in the east, *hrīṃ* in the south, and *śrīṃ* in the west. May *tu* protect me in the north.
May she who moves with wonder protect me in the southeast;
may she protect me in the southwest; may she protect me in the northwest; may she protect me in the northeast; I worship the sandals (pādukā);
likewise, may she always protect me above, in the half-moon, and in the prostration—thus has this armor (kavaca) been told to you, O beloved.

If one recites the most wonderful mantra of the Guru and then chants this armor (kavaca), he, along with his attendants, becomes a perfected being (siddha) and is none other than Śiva himself; of this there is no doubt. Furthermore, for one who recites this armor, which is the very embodiment of the mantra, at the time of worship, the full fruit of that worship shall accrue to him.
"Truly, truly, O Goddess of the Suras! O Goddess, he who recites this at the three junctions of the day becomes a perfected one (siddha); of this there is no doubt.

If one should write it according to the rules on birch bark and wear it placed within gold, by the mere sight of him, disputants are rendered lusterless; he obtains victory in debate and is victorious in battle."

He who recites this at the three junctions of the day while meditating upon the thousand-spoked wheel shall undoubtedly attain victory in the assembly; he becomes peerless, and having attained perfection in the worlds, he reaches the state of Nirvāṇa.
This most wonderful armor (kavaca), named "All-Auspiciousness," should not be given to just anyone.

It must never be given away nor revealed; it should be imparted to a disciple who is peaceful, otherwise one would become fallen. O Goddess of Gods, this is not given even to sons, except to one who is devoted.
If one recites this tenfold Vidyā without knowing this secret instruction, its fruit will be exhausted.
Otherwise, one may go to hell at the end; thus concludes the armor-mantra (*kavaca*), O Goddess. What else do you wish to hear?

Out of love for you and out of deference to you, what have I not revealed? Having first uttered the *kūrma* seed-syllable, O Beloved, [one should recite] the *prāśa* mantra; by means of this, during the conjunction with the wind (*vāyuyoga*).

The wise one should not perform the *nakuṇḍalīcakra* [without first] reciting the root mantra one hundred and eight times; then, having performed the rite of drinking [the nectar], he should perform the twilight worship (*sandhyā*) with a satisfied mind. Śrī Devī said: O Supreme Lord, tell me what kind of meditation (*dhyāna*) is to be practiced during the twilight worship. O Lord, let the specific details regarding the Śrīvidyā, even those that are difficult, be told to me. Om.
Śrī Śiva said: One should meditate upon the goddess Sundarī, who exists in three forms as the seed-syllables (bījas).
One should indeed meditate upon the goddess Vaiṣṇavī, whose essential form is white in color. One should contemplate the Kāma-bīja as being blue in color, and the Śakti-bīja as golden.
One should contemplate her as red in color at dawn, white in color at midday, and resembling blue in color at sunset;
at twilight, the best of practitioners should contemplate her as red in color.
Having meditated thus, O Great Goddess, the wise one should perform the twilight rite (sandhyā) and the worship of Śiva.

Then, having performed [the preliminary rites], one should worship the Supreme Deity, Tripura, the supreme Vidyā, the great Vidyā who is devoted to her husband; for she never accepts worship without the worship of her Lord. Thus, O Great Goddess, [one should worship] first the Linga...

One should worship the five-syllabled [mantra] and worship the five-faced [deity] with great effort; thereafter, one should worship the Goddess Tripura, the bestower of liberation. [Thus speaks] Śrī Devī.

"O Śaṅkara, tell me, out of compassion, upon what should one place the *śumbha*? O Goddess of Devas, tell me how the practitioner becomes a partaker of the fruit through the various types of supports.
Om, Śrī Śaṅkara said: Om, one should worship the earthen [liṅga]."

O Goddess, the linga may be made of stone, or likewise of gold, silver, copper, or bell-metal; it may be made of mercury, from the Gaṅgā, crystal, or even of glass— or by its various distinctions, O Mistress of Gods, it may be fashioned from sacred ashes.

One should worship a liṅga fashioned from sand or from cow dung; I shall now describe the consecration (saṃskāra) which pertains to the Supreme Lord Śiva. Having placed a silver or golden liṅga within a golden vessel, one should immerse that small liṅga in the midst of milk for three days.
Having installed Tryambaka, one should worship Kālarudra with the sixteen types of service (upacāras);
likewise, one should perform the recitation (japa) according to the lunar day (tithi).
Then, having lifted that linga from there, one should cast it into the waters of the Gaṅgā; thereafter, [one should proceed] according to the ritual manual (vidhi).
The wise one should perform the consecration according to the prescribed rite. Om. Caṇḍikā said:
Oṃ! O Lord of Devas, who speaks of the dimensions of the liṅga, O Sovereign, even if there should be a specific distinction regarding the earthen liṅga and so forth—Oṃ Śrī Śiva!

O Pārvatī, one should take either one *tolaka* or two *tolakas* of clay; it should be prepared with great care, never otherwise. O Lord of Devas, on the supreme stone slab which bestows fruits, one should fashion [the image] the size of a thumb.

O Goddess of the gods, the fruit of the Rudrākṣa becomes manifold according to its size, ranging from two joints upwards; O Supreme Goddess, O Goddess, the fruit of worshipping and wearing the Rudrākṣa— whether it be a large or even larger Liṅga— is considered to be of many kinds.
Thus ends the seventh chapter of the glorious Mātṛkā-tantra, complete. Oṃ saṃ 39 bhāvati 3. This was written by me, Kaulemukunda, on the moon [day].

Just as the manuscript was seen, so has it been written by me. If it is pure—*Oṃ śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ*. *Oṃ śrīśiva uvāca*: *Oṃ athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi tripurāmantram uttamam; yasya vijñānamātreṇa punarjanma na vidyate.* [The manuscript was written exactly as it was seen. If it is pure—*Oṃ obeisance to the illustrious Gaṇeśa*. *Oṃ the illustrious Śiva said*:
*Oṃ now, therefore, I shall fully declare the supreme mantra of Tripurā, by the mere knowledge of which rebirth is no longer found.]*
Those three forms of the Goddess Tripurā are Bagalā, Tripurā, and Śivā; likewise there is the goddess Bhairavī, who is declared to be composed of those very goddesses.
Now, O Pārvatī, listen with reverence to the goddess Bhairavī. [Thus spoke] Śrī Caṇḍikā: "O Lord, the great mantra has been heard from the Ḍāmara."
In the *Vīrayāmala*, [Śaṅkara] said: "Tell me the sequence of worship beginning with the morning rites.

Rising again, the knower of mantras should worship his own Guru in the thousand-spoked [lotus] with great effort, by means of the meditation previously described; and likewise, the meditation on the venerable Guru.
O fair-faced one, I have previously taught you only the secret practice; now hear the mantra.
Having extracted the Great Māyā preceded by the Vāgbhava [Bīja], which is the power of Viṣṇu, then follow the mantra of Ānandabhairava: *Ha Sa Kha Pha Raṃ*. After that is the mantra of his Śakti.

And it was said [by him] previously, O Lord: "Now let the hymn of praise (*stotra*) and the armor-verse (*kavaca*) of the venerable Guru also be told, by the mere speed of whose wings a person is liberated from *saṃsāra*. Om, salutations to you, O Lord of the gods of gods; salutations to you, O you who are worshipped by Hara, O Brahma-vī..."

Constant salutations to this one who possesses the form of a yoginī; salutations to that venerable Guru by whom the eye of one blinded by the darkness of ignorance was opened with the medicinal ointment-stone of knowledge;
[salutations] to her who dwells on the left side of the illustrious Lord, who is compassionate and worshipped by the gods.

Salutations again and again to her who is the eternal bestower of true knowledge; salutations again and again to that Goddess who, in the thousand-petaled great lotus, is the embodiment of eternal bliss and the giver of the great liberation;
she who is the very form of Brahmā and Viṣṇu, and the embodiment of the Great Rudra.

Salutations again and again to her whose nature consists of the three *guṇas*, who is impermanent; salutations again and again to her who has the forms of the moon, sun, and fire, whose eyes are ever-rolling, and who embraces her own Lord. Salutations to the one who is the life of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and others, while yet living.

Salutations again and again to her who bestows the supreme state and grants both knowledge (*jñāna*) and realization (*vijñāna*). O Maheśānī, he who recites this hymn with devotion shall truly obtain prosperity; this is the truth, this is the eternal truth—salutations again and again. He who recites it at dawn, preceded by the worship of the Guru, [attains the same].
O Goddess, in this world, service and sons are desired; the hymn of praise is now complete.
Now listen with reverence to the armor-vidyā (*kavaca*) of the Goddess, by the mere remembrance of which one attains equality with Vāgīśa (Brahmā).
Sadāśiva is the seer (*ṛṣi*) of this very armor-vidyā of the Śrī Guru.
The deity named Rsmṛta, who bestows the fruits of the four aims of life, has been proclaimed;

may the seed-syllable *klīṃ klīṃ* protect my head, and that which is named after it [the deity] protect my forehead. May the seed-syllable *klīṃ* protect my eyes, and may it always protect all my limbs. May the seed-syllable *eṃ* protect my... [mouth].
If it is impure, the fault of "Vāma" is not incurred. Om. [This concludes. Om.
The Śrīmātṛkātantra is complete. (Unpublished)
